The exercise states these without proof; this item supplies full half-line distortion and endpoint-circle calculations and proves its own smooth circle example.

The source calls the extension smooth, which is false for general quasisymmetric data; this item proves C1 regularity and records an odd square-root counterexample. Exercise 15.5 supplies the omitted technical calculations.

Ch. 2 §15.2.2 Lemma 15.6, printed pp. 208-209: the circle version of the Ahlfors-Beurling theorem. Its restriction direction requires |H(0)|<=r<1; the scaffold omitted this normalization, contradicted by disk automorphisms with K=1. The item supplies a periodic-lift proof of the extension and proves the normalized restriction statement by reflection and the global plane quasisymmetry bound.

alternatives.argument: The existing item proves its entire finite chordal-H1 claim independently in six steps. A Möbius chart moves the compact exceptional set away from infinity and compares chordal with Euclidean H1. At each vanishing scale a countable Hausdorff cover yields, by compactness, finitely many open squares with uniformly bounded side sum. Assigning overlap regions to their first square and subdividing gives polygon cells of diameter tending to zero, total perimeter at most twice the original perimeter sum, and cancellation of all internal oriented edges. The outer boundary of the union misses the exceptional set. Cauchy on the exterior region identifies the error in the outer Cauchy integral with the sum of cell-boundary integrals. Subtract a constant on each complete cell boundary; uniform continuity bounds this sum by the bounded total perimeter times a modulus of continuity tending to zero. The exceptional set has area zero from the same Hausdorff-cover estimate, so continuity extends the Cauchy formula across it. The function is entire and bounded by sphere compactness; Liouville makes it constant. No holomorphicity within the covering cells, disjoint original-square cover, Garnett theorem, or cited proof fallback is assumed.

alternatives.argument: All notions are defined locally by QC images with the same rich hypotheses: quasicircle is a chartwise orientation-preserving K-QC sphere image of the unit circle, quasidisk a corresponding disk image, quasiarc and quasiline plane QC images of the open segment and real line, and the constant is the infimum without an attainment assertion. The existing proof has two complete steps: composing the quotient-circle parametrization with a homeomorphism gives a Jordan embedding; Jordan separation and the exact partition into disk/exterior images give its two complementary quasidisks. Inversion is conformal on the sphere, so composing with it preserves K and realizes the exterior as a disk image. Möbius postcomposition and its inverse preserve the QC bound by the earlier proved composition theorem. Hence the admissible K sets for a curve and its Möbius image agree, so their infima agree. The stipulations for quasiarc/quasiline require no existence or characterization theorem from Martin. Lyubich printed209–211, §§15.3.1/15.3.4, actually read from the cached full-book extraction, corroborates quasicircle terminology and its QC-image formulation; its forward extension proof is not printed there and is not imported. This alternative uses only the retained item's established supplier interfaces, not an unread external proof.

sources.title: Lars V. Ahlfors, Quasiconformal reflections, Acta Mathematica 109 (1963), 291–301
sources.locator: Part I §§2–5, printed English Acta pp. 294–297 (Mathnet translation pp. 105–108): the controlled-length replacement of a reflection, Theorem 1’s three-point/cross-ratio characterization, and the complete necessity/sufficiency argument through extremal distances and the Beurling–Ahlfors extension.

contents.name: Part I §§2–5, printed pp. 294–297: quasiconformal reflection iff the three-point condition (for curves through infinity) or the equivalent alternating cross-ratio condition; proof derives the quasisymmetric boundary correspondence from complementary extremal distances

sources.title: Christopher J. Bishop, Some homeomorphisms of the sphere conformal off a curve, Annales Academiæ Scientiarum Fennicæ Mathematica 19 (1994), 323–338
sources.locator: Theorem 2, printed p. 324, and its construction in §§3–4, printed pp. 330–334: for each gauge h(t)=o(t), the construction yields a non-Möbius sphere homeomorphism conformal off a Jordan curve Γ with Λ_h(Γ)=0. Taking h(t)=t² gives zero 2-dimensional Hausdorff measure and hence zero planar area. The final conformal-filling step is described briefly; this theorem is a nonessential comparison, not an input to the disk witness.

contents.name: Theorem 2 and proof, printed pp. 324, 330–334: flexible nonremovable Jordan curves with zero Hausdorff gauge measure; h(t)=t² gives a zero-area nonremovable Jordan curve.

sources.locator: §3.2 Theorem 3.5; §4.2 Proposition 4.4; §5.1 Propositions 5.1 and 5.3; §5.2 Theorem 5.17; §5.4 Proposition 5.23 and Corollary 5.24, printed pp. 232–249.

contents.name: §3.2 Theorem 3.5 and §5.1 Propositions 5.1 and 5.3, printed pp. 232–233 and 241–242: finite-H¹ sets are A-removable (Theorem 3.4 is explicitly a sketch); A-removable sets are CH-removable (Proposition 5.1, referring to the quotient proof of Proposition 4.3 on pp. 235–236); CH-removability is QC-invariant (Proposition 5.3)
§5.1 Proposition 5.3 and Corollary 5.4, printed pp. 241-242: CH-removability is invariant under quasiconformal maps, and quasicircles are CH-removable

§5.2 Theorem 5.15, printed pp. 243–244: Carleson–Gehring product sets F×[0,1] are nonremovable iff F is uncountable; the item uses its own positive-area fat-Cantor product and not this zero-area product-set construction.
contents.reason: The B item directly constructs a positive-area empty-interior product from Smith–Volterra–Cantor sets, so it does not use the separate Carleson–Gehring theorem for uncountable compact null subsets of the line.

contents.name: §5.2 Theorem 5.17 and proof sketch, printed pp. 244–246: Bishop’s theorem giving nonremovable Jordan curves of zero gauge measure for every gauge h(t)=o(t); used only for the zero-area comparison remark. Full construction is checked in Bishop’s original paper.

§5.4 Proposition 5.23 and Corollary 5.24, printed pp. 248–249: equal welding classes give a homeomorphism conformal off the first boundary; a CH-removable boundary makes the Jordan domain unique up to Möbius. The proof is read in full.

contents.name: §2.1, printed p. 222: a single point and every finite set are removable for bounded holomorphic functions by Riemann's theorem; this is a distinct scalar-valued class from CH-removability
